title: Elric's Wobbly Charm
markdown:
High up in the craggy shoulders of the Misty Kettle mountains lived a young wizard named Elric. Knobby knees that always seemed to bump into things. Hair like he’d just wrestled a very happy cloud. Fingers smudged with a rainbow of potion-ink. He loved Misty Kettle: wind that whispered secrets only the oldest trees knew, heather that smelled like warm buttery biscuits. In his tummy a tiny fluttery butterfly told him his magic wasn’t quite as bright or as strong as it should be. Quiet. But there.

He wasn’t the only young magic-maker. Fen the witch had hair the colour of a fiery sunset, wild wonderful curls, a laugh like tiny tinkling bells. Clever, like Elric. Maybe a little cleverer about which mushroom made you giggle and which made you sing opera. Every year, as autumn leaves turned red, they had a contest. Not storms. Not badgers into teacups. Who could polish their charm to the shiniest most dazzling gleam.

“This year,” Elric told a stubborn patch of clover, “my charm will outshine Fen’s. It will gleam like a star that’s had a bath in moonlight.” He gathered his finest polishing pebbles, smooth and grey, polished by streams for ages. A special velvet cloth, soft as a sigh, moonbeam threads. His favourite mossy rock, as comforting as a warm hug. Wind sighed like a sleepy giant. “Right then,” he whispered to his cloudy charm. “Let’s make you sparkle like a new penny.”

He rubbed and buffed. Velvet. Gentle puffs. The charm stayed cloudy, a foggy window. He tried a warming charm, a tiny whisper of warmth. A smoothing spell. Instead of shining, the charm wobbled, as if trying a little jig. “Oh, bother.” The butterfly gave an energetic flutter. “My magic isn’t working right. It’s all wobbly.”

Squawk. A very round puffin waddled right up to the rock. Elric decided he must be named Percy. Beady black eyes on the pebbles. A mighty flap. Pebbles scattered down the hill like grey marbles at a game. “Percy. You cheeky bird.” A chuckle escaped. Unexpected. A little bit funny.

The pebbles mixed with bright wildflowers and soft green moss. They looked quite happy there.

Down the mountain, Fen’s fiery hair a bright spark. Her charm already gleaming, a bright light dancing in the sun, pixie dust and morning dew. Elric’s tummy did a little somersault. “She’s doing so well. Her charm looks like a little sun.”

Soft white snowflakes began to drift, landing on hair and fuzzy moss. Not winter. A snowflake on his nose. Snowflakes on a sunny afternoon. They tickled, and landed on the charm, making shine harder to see. “Now what?” Discouraged. The world against his polishing.

A flash of brown fur zipped past his feet. Pip, the plump mountain hare, long ears perked, nose twitching. Pip paused, looked at Elric, then at the snowy wobbly charm. With a gentle nudge of a soft whiskery head he pushed Elric’s hand toward the velvet cloth. Not just rubbing hard. The way you rubbed. The rhythm.

Elric watched the gentle rhythmic nudges. Remembered his own hurried worried rubbing. The charm that wanted to wobble-dance. The silly out-of-season snowflakes. Slowly, a spark of understanding. Maybe his magic wasn’t meant to be perfectly smooth and predictable, like Fen’s. Maybe its sparkle was in its little wobbles.

He picked up a polishing pebble that had landed near bright blue mountainbells. Gentler rhythm, steady, soothing, as Pip had shown. He let the little wobbles be. He even made a silly charm, a little tickle of magic, to make the snowflakes disappear. They turned into tiny shimmering rainbows that danced a moment before fading. His charm did not gleam like a mirror. A warm friendly glow. A cozy light that hummed. Little highlights where light caught its unique slightly wobbly shape.

He found Fen, admiring her dazzling charm. “Look.” His voice filled with new confidence. Fen looked. Then she smiled, genuine and warm, bell-like laugh tinkling softly. “It’s different, Elric. It has character. It looks like it’s smiling.” She held up her own charm, incredibly shiny. “But yours looks like it’s happy.” A thoughtful twinkle in her eye.

Elric looked at his charm, then at Fen’s, then at Pip, munching contentedly on heather, nose twitching happily. The little butterfly in his tummy had stopped fluttering. It was now doing a gentle happy somersault, like a swimmer in a calm sea. He had polished his charm. He had faced his worries. His magic, like him, was allowed its wobble. Percy, somewhere down the slope, squawked as if he had meant the pebbles all along. The heather still smelled of biscuits. The charm hummed, which was how you knew a contest could end without a mirror and still gleam.
characters: Elric (young wizard with knobby knees and potion-ink fingers), Pip (a plump mountain hare)
author: StoryGen Community
